This profound valuation gap is reinforced by a price-to-book ratio of just 0.40x, with the stock priced at ₹ 0.40 against a book value of ₹ 1.01 [E2], heavily discounting the company relative to the sector benchmark P/B of 1.35x [E7]. Furthermore, the underlying profitability metrics severely outpace the broader industry, delivering a return on assets of 8% compared to the sector benchmark of 1.8% [E8], alongside a robust return on equity of 7.78% that beats the sector's 4.93% [E9]. The market capitalization stands at a modest ₹ 11.6 Cr [E3], and the stock currently languishes near the bottom of its valuation cycle at just 10% of the way up its 52-week range [E5], offering a striking entry point for value capture. This secular unprofitability deepens into a negative 1% median return on equity over the last 3 years [E26], aligning with official flags highlighting a low return on equity of -0.71% over that timeframe [E58]. Investors looking for cash returns will find none, as the dividend yield sits firmly at 0.00% [E4]. Furthermore, the fundamental earning power of the enterprise is modest at best, demonstrated by a meagre ROCE of 5.3% [E12]. Reflecting these deep-seated operational frailties, the market has punished the equity, leaving the stock languishing at a mere 10% of the way up its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the company trades at a low P/E of 5.08x compared to a sector benchmark of 20.02x [E1, E6], and features a price-to-book ratio of 0.40x against a sector benchmark of 1.35x [E2, E7].

Conceded: dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], and ROCE stands at 5.3% [E12]. However, the bear's reliance on these historical metrics ignores the sharp, current turnaround in profitability shown by a recent ROE of 8% [E27]. This current 8% return actually outperforms the sector benchmark of 4.93% [E9]. Furthermore, the business generates an ROA of 8%, drastically beating the sector benchmark of 1.8% [E8]. The market's decision to leave the stock at 10% of its 52-week range [E5] completely misprices a company trading at a deep discount of 0.40x book value against a 1.35x sector benchmark [E2, E7]. Finally, this operational outperformance is completely disconnected from a meager P/E of 5.08x, which sits miles below the sector benchmark of 20.02x [E1, E6].

Conceded: Jackson Investments Ltd trades at a P/E of 5.08x compared to a sector benchmark of 20.02x [E1, E6], and a price-to-book of 0.40x against a sector benchmark of 1.35x [E2, E7], alongside an ROA of 8% beating the sector's 1.8% [E8]. However, the bull's reliance on a single recent 8% ROE [E27] ignores the structural reality of a 10-year and 5-year median ROE of 0% [E24, E25] and a 3-year median ROE of -1% [E26], which is officially flagged as a negative 3-year low return of -0.71% [E58]. Conceded: the current ROE of 8.1% [E13] and the 8% figure [E27] surpass the sector benchmark of 4.93% [E9], but a single year of performance fails to override a multi-year history of zero or negative returns [E24, E25, E26]. Furthermore, the micro-cap market capitalization of ₹ 11.6 Cr [E3], combined with a stagnant dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], leaves investors with no cash return and a stock price pinned at just 10% of its 52-week range [E5]. Finally, this weak structural positioning is fully corroborated by a lackluster ROCE of just 5.3% [E12], proving that the low valuation multiples are an accurate reflection of chronic historical underperformance rather than a market mispricing.
